claims.claim: A small payment on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time, but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: For a promissory note, payment alone does not revive an already barred claim. Before the bar, any payment by the party to be charged on principal or interest due starts a new period; the statute sets no minimum amount.

claims.claim: Signing something on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: The content of the writing matters. A signed acknowledgment or promise can be evidence of a new or continuing contract; a signature alone does not settle the question.

claims.claim: The applicable limit is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Supported within the stated scope of debts subject to the four-year limit.

claims.claim: The four-year limit keeps running no matter what is paid or signed.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: Section 337 expressly allows extension under section 360.

claims.claim: It is safe to make a payment.
claims.quote: to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note, and to start the running of a new period of time
claims.note: A qualifying note payment before the bar can change the deadline.

claims.claim: It is safe to sign a payment plan.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: A plan may contain a signed acknowledgment or promise. The source gives no blanket assurance of safety.

flags.text: The claim that the period keeps running regardless of payment contradicts the new-period rule for qualifying promissory-note payments.
The stated scope includes debts both near and past the limit, but the draft omits the distinction between starting a new period before the bar and reviving a claim once barred.
The draft treats all debts, payments and signed writings alike. Section 360 distinguishes note payments from written acknowledgments or promises.
“You can safely” directs the reader to act without knowing the timing, the type of debt or the terms of the plan.
Paying near the limit or signing a plan containing an acknowledgment or promise can weaken a limitations defense.

result.summary: The four-year period is supported within scope; the assurance that paying or signing cannot affect it is not. The payment rule depends on whether the claim is already barred, and the effect of a signed writing depends on what it says.
